claude.sample_unit: neurologists (responses to 21 clinical vignettes; ChatGPT-4o run 10 times per case)

links.outcome: Guideline-adherent responses with vs without RAG grounding on curated clinical documents
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o with RAG 80.5% correct vs 72.9% without context; vs neurologists 66.5% (p=0.001 with RAG; p=0.038 without). GEE OR 3.17 with RAG vs 1.55 without.
links.quote: Without context (mean: 72.9% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.038) and with context (mean: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001)

links.outcome: Guideline-adherent decisions of ChatGPT-4o compared with practicing neurologists on the same vignettes
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o with RAG 80.5% vs neurologists 66.5% (p=0.001); OR 3.17 (95% CI 2.05-4.88); no difference in NewFeeLs-MS sNfL scenarios.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o with RAG achieved significantly higher guideline adherence in decision-making than neurologists (80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT responses across 10 repeated runs per case
links.effect: Responses highly consistent across 10 repetitions, identical in most scenarios or showing minimal variability, typically two response patterns; some cases at 60-90% correct.
links.quote: In general, ChatGPT's responses were highly consistent across the 10 repetitions per case, with the model producing identical answers in most scenarios or showing minimal variability, typically limited to two different response patterns.

links.outcome: Correctness of LLM treatment recommendations in emerging-biomarker (sNfL) scenarios
links.effect: In NewFeeLs-MS, ChatGPT was 0% correct in 4-5 of 7 cases; mean 28.6% without context and 41.4% with context vs neurologists 54.2%, no significant difference.
links.quote: Conversely, for the NewFeeLs-MS study, no significant differences were observed in the percentage of correct responses between ChatGPT-4o and neurologists, either without context (mean: 28.6% vs. 54.2%; p = 0.191) or with context (mean: 41.4% vs. 54.2%; p = 0.518)

links.effect: ChatGPT higher overall: without context 72.9% vs. 66.5% (p = 0.038); with context 80.5% vs. 66.5% (p = 0.001).
links.quote: When analyzing results across all studies combined, ChatGPT-4o demonstrated a significantly higher percentage of correct responses than neurologists in both conditions: Without context (mean: 72.9% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.038) and with context (mean: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001) ( Figure 1A ).

links.effect: With RAG: PREFERENCES-NMOSD and DIScUTIR MS 100%; NewFeeLs-MS cases 1/5 100%, case 2 90%, remaining cases 0%.
links.quote: When ChatGPT was provided with context, a slight improvement in performance was observed, resulting in a 100% correct response rate across all evaluated cases for the PREFERENCES-NMOSD and DIScUTIR MS studies, while in NewFeeLs-MS, correct responses were observed in 100% of the iterations for cases 1 and 5, in 90% for case 2, and 0% in the remaining cases ( Table 3 ).

links.effect: 10 repetitions per case; identical answers in most scenarios; minimal variability, typically two response patterns.
links.quote: In general, ChatGPT's responses were highly consistent across the 10 repetitions per case, with the model producing identical answers in most scenarios or showing minimal variability, typically limited to two different response patterns.

links.outcome: correct responses in emerging biomarker scenarios
links.effect: NewFeeLs-MS: ChatGPT 28.6% without context and 41.4% with context vs. neurologists 54.2%; p = 0.191 and 0.518.
links.quote: Conversely, for the NewFeeLs-MS study, no significant differences were observed in the percentage of correct responses between ChatGPT-4o and neurologists, either without context (mean: 28.6% vs. 54.2%; p = 0.191) or with context (mean: 41.4% vs. 54.2%; p = 0.518) ( Figure 1D ).

links.outcome: Guideline-adherent treatment decisions with retrieval-augmented generation versus unaugmented prompt
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o adherence increased from 72.9% without context to 80.5% with context (versus 66.5% for neurologists, p=0.001), with multivariable odds ratio of 3.17 (p<0.0001) versus clinicians.
links.quote: When analyzing results across all studies combined, ChatGPT-4o demonstrated a significantly higher percentage of correct responses than neurologists in both conditions: Without context (mean: 72.9% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.038) and with context (mean: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001) ( Figure 1A ).
